sources.supports: Portal VM creation sequence, subscription and resource-group selection, image and size review, administrator SSH public-key setup, and deployment validation. The lesson deliberately replaces the quickstart's public access with an already approved private path.

sources.title: Check vCPU quotas
sources.supports: Regional and VM-family vCPU quota tiers, allocated and deallocated usage, Usage + quotas inspection, and the distinction between quota and actual regional or zonal capacity.

sources.title: Change the size of a virtual machine
sources.supports: Resize restarts and possible deallocation, persistent OS/data disks, Windows temporary-disk category restrictions, SCSI versus remote NVMe restrictions, and the requested-size model after allocation failure.

sources.title: Azure managed disks overview
sources.supports: Managed block storage, OS/data/temporary roles, VM-dependent disk support, disk backup concepts, temporary-disk loss scenarios, and managed-disk availability integration.

sources.title: Attach a managed data disk to a Windows VM
sources.supports: Portal creation and attachment, guest Disk Management initialization and formatting, verifying disk identity and LUN, destructive-operation warnings, and GPT for disks of two TiB or larger.

sources.title: Expand virtual hard disks attached to a Windows virtual machine
sources.supports: Separate Azure disk and guest volume expansion, unsupported shrinking, deallocation and online-expansion distinctions, and the four-TiB crossing restriction for Standard HDD, Standard SSD, and Premium SSD data disks.

sources.title: Ephemeral OS disks for Azure VMs
sources.supports: Disposable local OS writes, stateless-workload suitability, image/local-storage fit, reprovisioning after resize or redeploy, unsupported stop-deallocate lifecycle, snapshots, Backup, and Site Recovery, and distinction from temporary disks.

sources.title: Server-side encryption of Azure Disk Storage
sources.supports: Default managed-disk SSE, platform and customer keys, host-encryption boundary and cache-key behavior, guest ADE comparison, host-encryption restrictions, and customer-managed-key cross-subscription disk-move restrictions.

sources.title: Enable encryption at host using the Azure portal
sources.supports: EncryptionAtHost registration, supported-size checks, portal disk settings, existing-VM deallocation and reallocation, current or previous ADE incompatibility, 512e disk creation-date restriction, and scale-set existing-instance handling.

sources.title: Azure Disk Encryption for Windows VMs
sources.supports: Verified September 15, 2028 ADE retirement, failure to unlock after reboots following retirement, migration including backups, new-VM host-encryption recommendation, and warning against direct BitLocker decryption of ADE disks.

sources.title: Availability sets overview
sources.supports: Availability-set versus zone resilience, fault and update domain purposes, up-to-three fault and up-to-twenty update domains, region-dependent managed-disk domain counts, immutable configured counts, and deployment sequencing that can produce shared fault domains.

sources.title: Orchestration modes for Virtual Machine Scale Sets
sources.supports: Creation-time immutable orchestration mode, standard Flexible versus scale-set-specific Uniform VM management, supported autoscale and health integrations, fault-domain spreading qualifications, explicit Flexible outbound access, and distinct automatic OS-image support.

sources.title: Configure rolling upgrades on Virtual Machine Scale Sets
sources.supports: Current dedicated requirements for Flexible Application Health extension and Uniform extension or probe, manual-first health validation, batch percentages, pauses, unhealthy thresholds, and distinction between model upgrade policy and automatic OS-image upgrades.

sources.title: Understand autoscale settings
sources.supports: Minimum and maximum bounds, safe default capacity, instance and time aggregation, divide-by-instance queue normalization, per-rule cooldown since the most recent scaling action, any scale-out versus all scale-in conditions, and flapping avoidance.

sources.title: Move resources to a new resource group or subscription
sources.supports: Unchanged physical location, changed resource IDs, same-tenant subscriptions, permissions, temporary management locks, destination providers and quotas, validation, role-assignment handling, and consolidated cross-subscription dependencies.

sources.title: Special cases when moving virtual machines
sources.supports: VNet dependency requirements, availability-set grouping, Standard frontend scale-set restrictions, Marketplace plans, encryption, scheduled patching, and backup configurations that require extra move planning.

sources.title: Move Azure VMs across regions
sources.supports: Resource Mover setup permissions and identity, dependency validation, prepare/replicate/initiate/commit/discard workflow, source shutdown and downtime, target testing, supported combined-move capability, and separate source and helper-resource cleanup.

sources.title: Support for moving Azure VMs between regions
sources.supports: OS and security-type support including Windows versus Linux Trusted Launch, existing Site Recovery restriction, target-size comparison, excluded temporary disks, unretained regional public IP and peering, static-private-IP conditions, uncopied roles and extensions, and required outbound access.

sources.title: Known issues with managed identities for Azure resources
sources.supports: VM move stale managed-identity reference causing later startup failure, documented property-update workaround, and the separate effects of transferring subscriptions between Microsoft Entra directories.

lab.title: Optional manual lab: inspect one private VM and a disposable data disk
lab.purpose: Practice the separation between Azure resource configuration, guest storage, and application observations. This is an optional supervised exercise, not an automated deployment.
prerequisites: Use a teacher-approved nonproduction subscription, budget, and empty lab-only resource group. Do not use real student records or production credentials.
An administrator must grant permission to create and manage the lab VM, its disks and NIC, and use the approved subnet. The learner also needs guest administrator access for Windows Disk Management.
Arrange a working approved private RDP path, such as an existing supervised Bastion or VPN setup. Do not create a broad internet RDP rule to make the lab easier.
Have the administrator verify a supported Windows image, matching architecture and size, quota and capacity, and an already Registered EncryptionAtHost feature if host encryption is included.
Do not use an ADE-enabled or previously ADE-enabled VM. Keep all lab data fictional and disposable.
lab.costWarning: A created VM incurs compute and possibly OS licensing charges; disks, snapshots, networking, and Bastion can incur separate charges. Deallocating compute does not remove disk or other retained-resource charges. This lab uses no fixed price or free-tier promise.
steps: Before creating anything, record the chosen image, architecture, size, region, quota headroom, private subnet, managed OS disk, authentication method, and permitted spending window.

With explicit approval, manually create one private Windows test VM using the checked configuration and no VM public IP. If all host-encryption prerequisites are met, select Encryption at host during creation. Otherwise inspect the setting without claiming the protection is enabled.
Inspect deployment status, actual VM properties, NIC private address, and disk list. Connect through the prearranged private path and confirm the guest login separately from Azure portal access.

Manually create and attach one empty 32 GiB managed data disk. Record its name, size, and LUN; identify that exact empty device in Disk Management before initializing, formatting, and assigning an available letter.
Create a fictional text file on the new volume, read it back, and record its path. Identify any temporary storage separately without placing unique data there.

Optionally, within the approved charge limit, expand the data disk to 64 GiB using a supported workflow. Observe Azure's new device size, then extend the intended guest volume and confirm the original file remains readable.

Record the observed differences among VM power state, disk attachment, guest volume capacity, file access, and host-encryption configuration. Do not perform moves, scale-set creation, or a resize unless separately approved.
expectedResults: The VM can be managed through Azure and accessed through the approved private path, with network access and guest credentials tested separately.
The new disk is visible in Azure before its guest filesystem is prepared, and the fictional file resides on the intended persistent volume.
If expansion was performed, guest usable capacity increases only after the relevant volume is extended, without formatting the existing data.
Host encryption is reported as enabled only if registration, support, selected configuration, and resulting VM state were verified.
cleanup: Delete only the recorded lab VM and its lab-owned disks, NIC, and any lab-only ancillary resources after reviewing their delete-with-VM settings. Delete the lab resource group only if its contents have been confirmed to belong entirely to this exercise.
Check for retained unattached disks, snapshots, addresses, and other charged resources created by this exercise; remove only those no longer required and confirm deletion completes.
Do not delete shared VNets, Bastion, VPN gateways, identities, key stores, or backup resources. Do not remove shared subscription feature registrations as lab cleanup.
